column1: # The radiation that slice migration adds to a load of beamlets, the record pl-migration-radiation
# of docs/migration.md. Measured on 2026-11-12 with Lucifer at commit 31be058. Each row is the power
# of a run with run.migrate = true whose load has neither shot noise nor a seed field, as a fraction
# of the SASE power of the same configuration, which is the mean of 8 random seeds with migration
# off. The rows of sase are of the example examples/sase, which runs the Aramis line of
# examples/aramis.bmad, the Bmad translation of the lattice of Genesis4's Benchmark1-SASE. The rows
# LCLS and FLASH1 were recorded under the names of the two FEL lines, whose configurations in the
# program are the examples lcls and flash1, and the input files of those runs were not recorded. The
# columns line and wavelength_nm name the FEL line of a row and its radiation wavelength, as the
# figure and the table print them. The lattice and the beam of each line are in the table
# tab-mig-cases of the page. A row holds the lower and the upper end of the fraction over the
# positions from s_from_m to s_to_m, and one value in both columns where one value was recorded.
# Every value is as it was recorded on that day, with the digits it was recorded with.
# docs/figures/migration_radiation_figure.py reads this file. The columns are separated by tabs.
